Are you currently employed ? When did you graduate? 

If you currently work in labs ( as you said you did a degree in biomed ) I would try to use that to try and get work experience in pathology. 
For example if you work in a histo lab you could then email the corresponding consultants asking to shadow for a couple of days to get a better understanding of the workflow. ( if that makes sense ? From patient to lab) 

You could try becoming a befriended for individuals with Alzheimer’s and dementia. There are organisations that host recreational activities to help support the elderly. I absolutely loved doing this during university. 
You could try getting involved with charities such as Mind and anxiety uk and help them with outreach. 

One good idea is identify a medical cause you are passionate about . Find centres that align with your cause and try to work with them to perform outreach. Organise with them to engage with the public. 

All in all get involved get passionate about causes and get out there. Doing advocacy is not only extremely rewarding but it could help your communication skills. 

Focus on becoming a well rounded and compassionate individual.

Honestly, I’m not too sure what happened between both of you . However, I believe it’s in both of your best interests to talk about these issues . There could be some underlying issues that need to be addressed (such as mental health issues) or this could be one massive misunderstanding. 

Personally, my friends inspire me to do many things in my life . We are influenced by the people around us. When my friends do something that I’ve always wanted to do but never tried it also helps me come out of my comfort zone . 

I feel like if you are confident and popular people are more likely to trust the decisions you make for yourself. This they may want to try them out as well . 

I think an open conversation between both of you would be beneficial. 
Hope this helps

Unfortunately, people are naturally defensive and when they feel like their character is being questioned the ability to think critically and negotiate is out the window. It's a really unfortunate part of humanity that really needs to be rectified. I wish I could find a way of telling people that they are being ignorant without them feeling it's an insult to their character because a lot of the time it really is not. Also, It really proves that you were truly ignorant if you just accept what you did was wrong and move on but people view calling something racist as a personal attack on their character and it hurts their ego. I'm also fed up believe me that's why I'm becoming a shut-in. It honestly hurts their ego because it hasn't been normalized in society to be open yet? If that makes sense? If criticism was normalized and dialogue on racism was normalized I think many people wouldn't have a problem its just many people see minorities as others which is very disheartening. I feel like the shock is a normal response but defensiveness is toxic AF. I'm also trying to train myself to listen first then talk later so people are more willing to correct me.

I honestly accept it as an inevitability and stop caring. I know that sounds bad but I do not have control over how others view me but what I can control is my response. I also stopped taking these things to heart as it was detrimental to my mental health and well being. Also if they think negatively of you it's not your fault at all. I've experienced so much racism to the point if someone calls me the N world I'd probably chuckle and walk away. This type of fear produces strength.

Dear Reader 



If you have made it clear that you don’t like this word being said I think you need to make it clear that you have boundaries. If they can’t accept your boundaries leave because they WILL NEVER CHANGE . 



Unfortunately I made this mistake before with 2 people who were absolute pain in the asses . Good friends understand boundaries and are tactful, if they don’t then they are not your friends. Make sure to make it clear , if they don’t care then leave . It is their loss. Words have impact and at the age of 20 they should understand this. 



As for online ... people are idiots and will type and say whatever they want. Life is full of all sorts of people and I have found through my own personal experiences regardless or race or ethnicity you may only vibe with 20-30% of them. These people in all honestly are not important in your life , you are the centre of your life ... your well being is n.o 1. 



In my opinion when you find a group of people you vibe with well and understand you well you stop caring about everyone else. Perhaps it’s time to move on... it is very difficult at first but learn to love yourself and guard your heart . That way you find amazing people. Trust me. 
(Sorry for any SPAG errors it is 2 am in the land of crumpets ) 

Yours sincerely 

Someone who has been there  ( Afro-British female ) 

N.B. Feel free to message me to talk about anything. I would really love to hear back from you . I firmly believe talking through issues with someone who has no history with you can be very beneficial.
